title: Psalm 8 — The majesty of YHWH's name, and a mortal a little less than Elohim

verdicts.reasoning: lamnaṣṣēaḥ ʿal-haggittît mizmôr lĕdāwid, MT v 1: ASV terms kept; 'of David' preserves the ambiguity of lĕ-; LXX 'winepresses' recorded. MT numbering (superscription = v 1) verified against the source and the canon's 'Psaumes VIII-6'.

citations: Kraus, Psalms 1-59, ad loc. (text-critical note on 8:2b)
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed: ʾăšer tĕnâ hôdĕkā ʿal-haššāmāyim. MT tĕnâ is pointed as an impv. of ntn, which has no syntax after ʾăšer; the line reads the unchanged consonants as a perfect ('you who have set', ASV/NRSV). This is a vowel-only departure, recorded as the single exception in the MT-baseline entry, with the tnh 'recount' derivation given. It is defensible: the alternative is an English line with no grammar. 'skies' because v 4 names the same visible sky; 'in all the earth' for the universal formula.
mippî ʿôlĕlîm wĕyōnĕqîm yissadtā ʿōz lĕmaʿan ṣôrĕreykā lĕhašbît ʾôyēb ûmitnaqqēm: MT ʿōz 'strength' kept against LXX ainon (Matt 21:16), recorded. Exact.
kî-ʾerʾeh šāmeykā maʿăśê ʾeṣbĕʿōteykā yārēaḥ wĕkôkābîm ʾăšer kônāntâ: 'your skies' (physical sky with moon and stars); Polel kwn 'set in place'. Exact.
māh-ʾĕnôš kî-tizkĕrennû ûben-ʾādām kî tipqĕdennû: ʾĕnôš 'a mortal' / ben-ʾādām 'a son of human' (central ben-adam, whose rationale already cites this verse); pqd 'attend to'. Literal and lens-free.

Re-parsed: wattĕḥassĕrēhû mĕʿaṭ mēʾĕlōhîm (Piel ḥsr 'make lack'; min comparative; ʾĕlōhîm anarthrous). 'a little less than Elohim' leaves ʾĕlōhîm untranslated under the corpus rule and follows the Hebrew in having no article; the note gives ASV/NRSV 'God', LXX/Targum/Heb 2:7 'angels', NJPS 'divine' fairly. The reception note correctly states that no witness reads 'equal'. The line differs from the canon's wording ('the Elohim') and so cannot be read as canon-driven (founder point A).
tamšîlēhû bĕmaʿăśê yādeykā kōl šattâ taḥat-raglāyw: Hiphil mšl 'make rule'. Exact.
ṣōneh waʾălāpîm kullām wĕgam bahămôt śādāy: rare forms correctly identified. Exact.
ṣippôr šāmayim ûdĕgê hayyām ʿōbēr ʾorḥôt yammîm: 'the birds of the skies' (physical sky), collective participle. Exact.
YHWH ʾădōnênû māh-ʾaddîr šimkā bĕkol-hāʾāreṣ: inclusio of v 2a, rendered identically. Exact.

glossaryReview.reasoning: Philologically neutral and correctly direct: a typographic convention, with the Hebrew form standing in the source text and every name verified (David, Solomon, Jerusalem, Zion, Israel, Jacob, Job). Flagged only because it is founder point D (the corpus split with the Kings transliteration). Reviewer view: accept English forms for the Writings. Job 37 must match the stable job-woh chapters, which are not retro-edited, and the four books must agree with each other. Record the genre split (narrative transliterated, poetry English) as deliberate, or settle it corpus-wide in one later decision.

Every site verified: YHWH; 'Yah' (Ps 147:1, 20); the article follows the Hebrew (anarthrous Ps 8:6; Eccl 3:10, 13; articular Eccl 3:11, 14, 15, 17, 18); 'El', 'Eloah' and 'Shaddai' as in stable job-woh (38:41; 40:2, 9); 'our Lord' for ʾădōnênû. Direct is right: these are presentation rules over explicit Hebrew forms. Flagged only for founder point A (Ps 8:6 'Elohim' against the canon's 'the Elohim'). Reviewer view: keep the anarthrous form. The Hebrew has no article, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and the Kings clause 2, and departing from the canon's wording here is evidence that the line is not canon-driven.

Site-by-site application of the founder's Kings-wave register ruling, checked verse by verse: physical sky 'skies' (Ps 8:2, 4, 9; 19:2, 7; 33:6; 147:8; Prov 8:27; Eccl 3:1; Job 37:3); dwelling or cosmic height 'heavens' (Ps 33:13 || mĕkôn-šibtô; 139:8 against She'ol). Ps 8:2 ('splendor upon the skies') is the closest call and is argued from v 4. Direct is appropriate.

'earth' at universal and cosmic sites (kol-hāʾāreṣ; ʾereṣ || tēbēl) is the reading of ASV, NRSV and NJPS, and the isaiah-woh precedent. 'land' is kept for territory (Prov 10:30; Job 37:13) and the stable 'wings of the land' (Job 37:3 = 38:13). Every site was checked. Agree with founder point C: promote the clause to central eretz in a later diff.

The lexical mapping is accurate and consistent with central ha-adam / ben-adam (direct) and with GEN-WOH-11:5 'the sons of the human' (checked). ʾĕnôš 'a mortal' and ʾîšîm 'O men' are sound. Flagged for founder point B. The articular/anarthrous split ('the sons of the human' / 'the sons of human', Prov 8:4, 31) is formally exact but yields stiff English, and in Biblical Hebrew the two forms are not distinct in sense. The corpus is now split three ways ('sons of men' ASV / canon-EN; 'children of men' 1 Kgs 8:39; 'sons of the human' Gen 11:5). Reviewer view: accept the editor's forms for coherence with the central entries, and align 1 Kgs 8:39 to them. If the founder prefers idiom, revert all bĕnê (hā)ʾādām sites together to 'the sons of men' with a string swap, and leave the singular ben-adam untouched.

Applied correctly at every listed site. MT Psalm numbering was verified (superscription = v 1 in Pss 8, 19; run into v 1 in Ps 139). The one vowel-only exception at Ps 8:2 is declared and justified: the MT impv. tĕnâ has no syntax after ʾăšer. Eccl 3:21 keeps the Masoretic articular participles and fully records the interrogative reading of LXX, Vulgate, ASV, NRSV and NJPS. Non-blocking: add 'KJV' to the Eccl 3:21 clause as the English witness to the MT pointing ('the spirit of man that goeth upward'), so that the entry does not suggest that every English version departs from the MT.
The ASV terms are accurate, and the uncertainty is honestly stated: lamnaṣṣēaḥ (Piel ptc. nṣḥ), mizmôr, Gittith, and the ambiguity of lĕdāwid. Direct is appropriate.

The Hebrew mēʾĕlōhîm is anarthrous, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and Kings clause 2, and the reception note already gives the canon's 'the Elohim'. Differing from the canon here is useful evidence that the line follows the Hebrew.

The cost is stiff English at Prov 8:4, 31, and the Hebrew article on bĕnê (hā)ʾādām carries no difference in sense. i18n.en: For the Chief Musician; set to the Gittith. A Psalm of David.

notes.official: Superscription, counted as v 1 in the Masoretic numbering, so every verse of Ps 8 is one number ahead of the ASV (MT 8:6 = ASV 8:5; `mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`). The refIds and the canon's citation ('Psaumes VIII-6') follow the MT. *lamnaṣṣēaḥ* 'For the Chief Musician' (ASV; NRSV 'To the leader') is the Piel participle of *nṣḥ* 'direct, oversee'. *ʿal-haggittît* 'set to the Gittith' names an instrument or tune whose sense is lost (LXX 'over the winepresses', reading *gittôt*). *mizmôr lĕdāwid* 'A Psalm of David': *lĕ-* may mark authorship, dedication or a collection, and English 'of' keeps the ambiguity (`psalm-superscription-terms-psalms`; `proper-names-english-forms-convention-writings`).

paragraphs.text: יְהוָ֤ה אֲדֹנֵ֗ינוּ מָֽה־אַדִּ֣יר שִׁ֭מְךָ בְּכָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּנָ֥ה ה֝וֹדְךָ֗ עַל־הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: YHWH, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth, you who have set your splendor upon the skies!

notes.official:
*ʾăšer tĕnâ hôdĕkā ʿal-haššāmāyim* is the psalm's textual crux. The MT points *tĕnâ* as an imperative ('set!'), which does not construe after the relative *ʾăšer*. The line follows the ASV ('who hast set thy glory upon the heavens') and NRSV ('You have set your glory above the heavens'), which read the same consonants as a perfect of *ntn* (*nātattâ*); others derive the form from *tnh* 'recount' (cf. Judg 5:11), 'whose splendor is recounted above the skies' (Craigie, WBC 19, ad loc.). The consonants are unchanged. This is the one place in the wave where the line departs from the Masoretic vowels, and the departure is recorded under `mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`.

*šāmayim* is the visible sky over which the splendor is set, the same sky the speaker looks at in v 4, so the line has 'skies' under the register rule of the central `shamayim` entry (ASV 'heavens'; `shamayim-register-application-writings`). *YHWH ʾădōnênû* 'YHWH, our Lord' keeps the name and the title apart (`divine-names-convention-writings`). *bĕkol-hāʾāreṣ* 'in all the earth' is universal in scope, so the line has 'earth', not the central default 'land' (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`).

paragraphs.text: מִפִּ֤י עֽוֹלְלִ֨ים ׀ וְֽיֹנְקִים֮ יִסַּ֪דְתָּ֫ עֹ֥ז לְמַ֥עַן צוֹרְרֶ֑יךָ לְהַשְׁבִּ֥ית א֝וֹיֵ֗ב וּמִתְנַקֵּֽם׃

i18n.en: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings you have founded strength, because of your adversaries, to still the enemy and the avenger.

notes.official: *mippî ʿôlĕlîm wĕyōnĕqîm yissadtā ʿōz* 'Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings you have founded strength' (MT; ASV 'established strength'). The LXX has *ainon* 'praise' for *ʿōz*, the form quoted at Matt 21:16. The line keeps the MT (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`). *ʿōz* is strength and also a stronghold (BDB), which suits the military language of the second half ('adversaries', 'enemy', 'avenger').

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־אֶרְאֶ֣ה שָׁ֭מֶיךָ מַעֲשֵׂ֣י אֶצְבְּעֹתֶ֑יךָ יָרֵ֥חַ וְ֝כוֹכָבִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר כּוֹנָֽנְתָּה׃

i18n.en: When I see your skies, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars, which you have set in place —

notes.official: *šāmeykā* 'your skies', with the moon and the stars: the physical sky, so 'skies' under the central `shamayim` rule (ASV 'heavens'). *maʿăśê ʾeṣbĕʿōteykā* 'the work of your fingers'; *kônāntâ* 'you have set in place' (Polel of *kwn* 'establish, fix').

i18n.en: what is a mortal, that you remember him, and a son of human, that you attend to him?

notes.official: *māh-ʾĕnôš ... ûben-ʾādām* sets two words for humankind in parallel. *ʾĕnôš* is 'a mortal' (BDB 'man, mankind', often with a note of frailty), which keeps it distinct from *ʾādām*. *ben-ʾādām* is 'a son of human' under the central `ben-adam` entry, whose rationale already cites this verse (ASV 'man ... the son of man'; `adam-enosh-ish-human-terms-writings`). *tipqĕdennû* 'that you attend to him' (ASV 'visitest'): *pqd* is to take note of and care for. Heb 2:6 quotes the verse from the LXX ('son of man').

paragraphs.text: וַתְּחַסְּרֵ֣הוּ מְּ֭עַט מֵאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְכָב֖וֹד וְהָדָ֣ר תְּעַטְּרֵֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: Yet you have made him a little less than Elohim, and with glory and honor you crown him.

notes.official:
*wattĕḥassĕrēhû mĕʿaṭ mēʾĕlōhîm* 'Yet you have made him a little less than Elohim'. The Piel of *ḥsr* is 'cause to lack, make less' (ASV 'made him but little lower'). The referent of *ʾĕlōhîm* is the verse's old question. The ASV and NRSV have 'God'. The LXX *par' angelous* 'than the angels', followed by the Targum, the Vulgate, the KJV and Heb 2:7, takes it as the heavenly beings. NJPS ('little less than divine') and the NRSV margin ('than the divine beings') take it as a class. The line follows the corpus rule: *ʾĕlōhîm* is left untranslated (`elohim-as-translation`) and has no English article, because the Hebrew has none (`divine-names-convention-writings`, as job-woh 1:9 'fear Elohim'). 'Elohim' keeps the plural form visible and leaves the referent open, which none of the English alternatives does.

*wĕkābôd wĕhādār tĕʿaṭṭĕrēhû* 'and with glory and honor you crown him': royal vocabulary, which the dominion of vv 7-9 continues.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes the verse as 'a little lower than the Elohim' ('peu inférieur aux Elohim') and reads it as saying that humans are almost as strong intellectually as their creators. It adds that the copyists did not dare to write 'equal to the Elohim', as had been dictated. No Hebrew manuscript or ancient version reads 'equal', and the line renders the MT. The canon's wording differs from the line only in the English article, which the Hebrew does not have.

paragraphs.text: תַּ֭מְשִׁילֵהוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣י יָדֶ֑יךָ כֹּ֝ל שַׁ֣תָּה תַֽחַת־רַגְלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: You make him rule over the works of your hands; you have put all things under his feet:

notes.official: *tamšîlēhû* 'You make him rule' (Hiphil of *mšl*); *kōl šattâ taḥat-raglāyw* 'you have put all things under his feet'. The verse takes up the dominion of Gen 1:26-28, with *mšl* for the *rdh* of Genesis.

paragraphs.text: צֹנֶ֣ה וַאֲלָפִ֣ים כֻּלָּ֑ם וְ֝גַ֗ם בַּהֲמ֥וֹת שָׂדָֽי׃

i18n.en: sheep and oxen, all of them, and also the beasts of the field,

notes.official: *ṣōneh waʾălāpîm* 'sheep and oxen' uses rare poetic forms of *ṣōʾn* and *ʾelep*; *bahămôt śādāy* 'the beasts of the field' has the archaic *śāday* for *śādeh*.

paragraphs.text: צִפּ֣וֹר שָׁ֭מַיִם וּדְגֵ֣י הַיָּ֑ם עֹ֝בֵ֗ר אָרְח֥וֹת יַמִּֽים׃

i18n.en: the birds of the skies, and the fish of the sea, whatever passes through the paths of the seas.

notes.official: *ṣippôr šāmayim* 'the birds of the skies': the physical sky (`shamayim`). *ʿōbēr ʾorḥôt yammîm* 'whatever passes through the paths of the seas': the singular participle is collective, the creatures of the sea (cf. Gen 1:21).

i18n.en: YHWH, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth!

notes.official: The refrain of v 2a closes the psalm as an inclusio. 'In all the earth' as in v 2 (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`).
